subject: Model improvement carveouts & EU transfer mapping for HealthTek evaluation
messages:
From: Maya Torres <maya.torres@healthtek.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor DPA - model improvement carveouts and transfer questions

Camila —

Thanks again for the product demo last week. Our legal team reviewed Redwood's standard DPA and flagged a few items that are blockers for procurement on our side:

- Explicit, contract-level confirmation that HealthTek customer inputs and outputs will not be used to improve models (no-training/no-derive).
- Clear ownership language for prompts and generated responses — we need an unambiguous statement that responses are HealthTek property and that Redwood will not assert derivative rights.
- Subprocessor transparency: we need the full list of subprocessors and a description of what data they see, plus an assurance about transfers out of the EU (SCCs or EU-hosted processing).
- Evidence we can rely on: logs/audit artifacts proving isolation or proof that no-training commitments are enforced.

I attached our redlines and highlighted the relevant clauses. Can you confirm what evidence Redwood can provide, whether you can accept a no-train OSS for our environment, and whether routing EU traffic to EU regions is available for the pilot?

If helpful, Legal is open to a short sync Tuesday afternoon (we're PT).

Thanks,
Maya Torres
Senior Counsel — Privacy & Compliance
HealthTek
Attachment: HealthTek_DPA_redlines.docx

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Maya Torres <maya.torres@healthtek.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor DPA - model improvement carveouts and transfer questions

Maya —

Appreciate the clear list, and thanks for sharing the redlines. High-level response here and then a proposal for next steps:

Summary answers
- No-training: We can offer a contract-level "no-training" commitment scoped to customer-provided conversational data for HealthTek's production traffic. That means those inputs/outputs will not be used for model updates or training our base models.
- Derivative/IP: We can accept language that confirms HealthTek retains ownership of prompts and generated outputs; Redwood will not assert ownership over customer outputs.
- Subprocessors & transfers: We'll provide the current subprocessor registry (attached) and can map processing by region. For EU residency, we can route HealthTek EU traffic to our EU Dedicated region and sign SCCs where required.
- Evidence: We maintain an evidence pack (logs, KV isolation indicators, retention configs). We can produce a compact evidence bundle for procurement that demonstrates the enforcement controls.

Options for contract wording (to make redline work faster)
1) Full no-train commitment + limited audit evidence pack: Contract confirms no-training for named data classes and Redwood delivers an evidence bundle on request (logs + configuration snapshots).
2) Opt-out flag approach + telemetry proof: Instead of a global no-train, customers can enable a per-tenant opt-out setting at runtime (recommended for piloting some flows), and we provide audit logs proving the flag was respected.

Next steps
- I attached our subprocessor list (subprocessor_list_2025.csv) and a short clause mapping (HealthTek_response_clause_matrix.pdf) that shows proposed redlines for the DPA vs your edits.
- Would you and Legal take option 1 or option 2?
- If option 1, we can prepare an evidence packet and a clean DPA with the explicit no-training language for your team to review.

I'm available Tuesday 1–3pm PT for a quick sync. If Legal prefers, we can also do a short workshop to walk through the evidence artifacts and EU routing.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: subprocessor_list_2025.csv; HealthTek_response_clause_matrix.pdf

From: Maya Torres <maya.torres@healthtek.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, legal@healthtek.com
Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2025 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor DPA - model improvement carveouts and transfer questions

Camila —

Thanks for the quick reply and the attachments. A few follow-ups from Legal after an initial pass:

1) Evidence artifacts: Legal needs to see the types of logs/records you will produce. Specifically:
   - Audit trail showing the opt-out flag/tenant setting being set and respected for a production request.
   - A KV cache snapshot or logical description showing customer data is not flowed into training pipelines.
   - Retention configuration snapshots and deletion proof for a sample record.

2) Scope of no-training: We need the commitment to be explicit that it covers both prompts and responses for HealthTek accounts, across both hosted and any dedicated/private deployments we purchase.

3) EU transfers: SCCs are fine as a baseline, but we would prefer an operational guarantee that EU-person data for EU users is processed in the EU region for the pilot period. Can Redwood commit to routing EU traffic to EU Dedicated region for the pilot?

4) Subprocessors: the CSV is a good start. Legal will want to see which subprocessors have access to payload-level data vs telemetry-only. Can you annotate the list accordingly?

If you can provide a short evidence pack (example artifacts) and an annotated subprocessors CSV by Friday (19 Sep), we can get procurement and security comfortable and start DocuSign for the DPA next week. Also attaching a blank SCC template for orientation.

Best,
Maya
Attachment: SCC_template.docx

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model improvement carveouts & EU transfer mapping for HealthTek evaluation

Camila / Grace —

Looping in a quick internal plan so we can hit Maya's Friday ask and keep the sales cadence moving. Notes and action items:

- Commitment & scope: Offer the full contract no-training commitment scoped to HealthTek customer data (prompts + outputs) across Hosted and any Dedicated instances they purchase for the pilot. Add a clause that allows limited operational telemetry for abuse detection & billing but not model updates.

- Evidence pack: Prepare an "evidence_no_train_checklist.pdf" with the following artifacts:
   * Example audit entry showing tenant opt-out flag set and a matching request trace.
   * Snapshot of retention configuration in the customer's Dedicated namespace.
   * High-level diagram and config note proving no data is forwarded into training pipelines (redacted).
   * A signed attestation from Infra that subprocessors annotated as "payload access" are only in named regions.

- Subprocessors CSV: Annotate subprocessor_list_2025.csv with access level (payload | telemetry | metadata-only) and indicate which ones process in EU. Importance: Legal needs this explicit for SCC applicability.

- EU routing: Confirm routing to EU Dedicated region for pilot. Ops can provision a dedicated region for HealthTek trial with strict tenancy. I will coordinate SLA/ops kick-off.

- Contract approach: We'll prepare a clean DPA with the explicit no-training clause + our proposed redline showing the elimination of ambiguous model-improvement language. Also include optional language for a per-tenant opt-out flag if they want a runbook approach.

Action owners & timeline
- Camila: produce annotated subprocessor CSV and initial evidence bundle (due Fri 2025-09-19 EOD).
- Grace: coordinate with Ops to reserve EU Dedicated routing and produce a short note describing isolation guarantees (due Fri).
- Aditya: draft the DPA clean copy and redline for Legal review and prep DocuSign (due Mon 2025-09-22).

If we deliver these artifacts by Friday, we should be able to get HealthTek into DocuSign early next week and keep the procurement timeline intact.

Thanks — I know Legal is thorough here; let's keep the artifacts concise and operationally focused.

- Aditya
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
Attachment: evidence_no_train_checklist.pdf
